title: EKS provisioner Terraform module: immutable identifiers, canary upgrades, and health probes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Merge a new, production-ready Terraform module for provisioning Redwood Private EKS control plane and associated IAM/network resources with strong safety guarantees for rolling upgrades. The module must: (1) avoid accidental resource replacement by using stable/immutable IDs for critical resources; (2) expose a lightweight canary upgrade mechanism for node pools and instance fleets; (3) include automated health probes and readiness checks to gate rollouts; and (4) provide clear outputs for downstream automation (kubeconfig, cluster endpoint, control-plane logging ARN).

Context: Current private EKS provisioning code paths are split between an older provisioner and ad-hoc infra scripts. Past incidents (see ENG-11120) showed upgrade scripts can inadvertently replace control-plane adjacent resources, causing short outages. This ticket consolidates behavior into a single terraform module that prioritizes idempotency and safe upgrades while still supporting reserved/private networking and KMS-backed secrets.

Scope: terraform module (module/eks_controlplane) + CI terratest wrapper + docs/example for private and dedicated customers. Not in scope: changes to Dedicated autoscaling policies (that is a follow-up), or support for on-prem air-gapped non-AWS clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Module applies cleanly (terraform apply) in a staging account and produces no resource replacements on repeated applies unless inputs change intentionally
Module exposes a parameter 'canary_ratio' (0.0-1.0) that, when set, performs a staged nodegroup replacement where at most canary_ratio of desired capacity is replaced first

Pre-upgrade and post-upgrade health probes run automatically in CI and block promotion on failures (probe checks: kube-apiserver readiness endpoint, control-plane logs ingestion, and API latency SLOs)
Outputs include kubeconfig (s3 path reference), cluster_endpoint, cluster_oidc_arn, node_groups (map of names to ARNs), and terraform-managed immutable_ids used for drift detection
Module includes clear migration notes and an automated migration helper script for existing clusters that used the old provisioner
Unit+integration tests (terratest) pass in CI and a runbook is documented for manual rollback steps
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with infra, security, and PM. Agreed on managed node groups for first rollout (reduce maintenance burden) and to model immutable_ids using a stable salt + cluster_id strategy.

2026-02-27: Added terraform output schema draft and example; security requested KMS key rotation notes and audit IAM role separation. Opened proposal doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/EKS+Provisioner+Module+Proposal

2026-03-02: Implemented initial canary flow using lifecycle create_before_destroy=false + explicit extra nodegroup for canaries. Trade-off: more temporary capacity during rollout vs simpler deterministic rollback. Documented cost impact.
2026-03-05: First terratest passing locally (kind->eks simulated) for idempotent apply path. Filing PR: https://github.com/redwood-infra/terraform-eks-provisioner/pull/204
2026-03-08: Design review feedback from Security: require encryption-in-transit checks, add 'security_review_required' flag to module usage. Implemented KMS key module hook and audit role separation.

2026-03-10: Reviewers requested stronger health gating (API latency + kube-apiserver cert fingerprint check). Added probe implementation using aws-cloudwatch metric filters for apiserver latency and a small Lambda that validates API cert thumbprint during rollout.
2026-03-12: PR updated with fixes, CI terratest runs in progress. Planning a canary deploy to staging cluster on 2026-03-16 pending signoff. Next: finalize rollback automation and update runbook.
next_steps: Complete CI terratest matrix across three instance types and two kubernetes versions (1.25, 1.26)
Run staged canary on staging cluster 2026-03-16 and validate probe metrics for 48 hours
Finalize rollback helper and add a 'promotion' GitHub Action that only runs when health gates pass
Create migration helper for clusters created by older provisioner and schedule a migration window with SRE
